clue.text: 'Crumbling gable' artist's symbolic subject

indicators.note: a crumbling gable falls apart, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A painter's title for a picture of a decaying gable end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' rearranges GABLE into ALGEB; the quotation marks dress it up as a painting's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics that works with symbols standing for numbers.

clue.text: Acknowledges obsolete currency in islands

indicators.note: the currency is placed in the islands, inside their letters

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
DM is the Deutschmark, replaced by the euro

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to holding old money on some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess or acknowledge it as true.

clue.text: Groups retrospectively brought in by fare negotiators

indicators.note: looking back, the held letters are read in reverse order
the answer is brought in by the words, held within their run of letters

explanation.surface: Groups of passengers whose fares were renegotiated after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading back through faRE NEGotiators gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are taxonomic groups of related species.

clue.text: Dealing with buzzers sounding alert — I'm scared to enter

indicators.note: the cry of fright is told to enter, so it goes inside the alert sound

parts.note: beeping is an alarm sounding
eek! is a squeal of fright

explanation.surface: Panic as an alarm goes off and a frightened person must go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzers' suggests alarm devices; they are bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Beekeeping is the tending of bees, the insects that buzz.

clue.text: Lark averse to cold?

parts.note: anti means opposed or averse to
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A songbird that dislikes winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' looks like the bird; it is a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful caper, which is also what a lark is.

clue.text: Spot storyline with school setting

indicators.note: a school setting holds the storyline like a jewel's mount, so the school abbreviation goes round it

parts.note: a plot is the storyline of a book or film

explanation.surface: Someone describing a novel whose plot takes place in a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a large irregular spot or blot of colour.

clue.text: Stratford flower seller, America's rising star

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from the bottom up, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows: the River Avon runs through Stratford
a rep is a sales representative
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A florist in Stratford becomes an American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes and briefly blazes very brightly.

clue.text: Two gents on air possibly a wonderful thing

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, so it is the spoken sound that counts

parts.note: gents is British slang for a men's toilet, a loo, and two of them give loo-loo

explanation.surface: Two men broadcasting something marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' suggests men, but in Britain the Gents is a men's lavatory, also a loo.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is an informal word for a remarkable or outstanding example of something.

clue.text: See 14
Mimic successfully adopting new technology to get on

indicators.note: the phrase adopts, takes in, the technology, so those letters go inside

parts.note: to hit off a person is to imitate them well
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Copying well by taking up a new gadget in order to progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit it off is an idiom for getting on well with someone from the start.

clue.text: Living accommodation north of the border

definitions.text: Living accommodation north of the border

parts.words: Living accommodation north of the border
parts.note: a 'living' is a church benefice, so this is a minister's house in Scotland, north of the English border

explanation.surface: Talk of housing in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living' reads as everyday life, but here it is a clergy post; north of the border means Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially of the Church of Scotland.

clue.text: First-rate access to attic?

definitions.meaning: the ... of stairs in a house leads up to the attic

explanation.surface: Praising the best way of getting up into a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight is an idiom for excellent; literally, the highest staircase gives entry to the roof space.

clue.text: Secret hero, roughly sixty

indicators.note: roughly handled, the letters are knocked about into a different order

explanation.surface: An undercover hero aged about sixty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like it qualifies sixty, but it is the anagram signal for SECRET HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty, an old-fashioned count of years.

clue.text: Figure from report incomplete

indicators.note: an incomplete word is missing its final letter, so the synonym is cut short at the end

parts.note: to state something is to report it

explanation.surface: A number quoted from an unfinished document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a noun but is the verb STATE, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat is an informal short form of statistic, a numerical figure.

clue.text: Cat beetled off before one's very eyes

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat scuttled away right in front of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beetled off' reads as hurried away; 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: What is detectable can be noticed or perceived, as if visible in plain sight.

clue.text: Draw with number one in league to regain control

parts.note: to pull is to draw or drag
looking after number one means looking after oneself
people in league are working together

explanation.surface: A sports team drawing a match while top of the league, then steadying itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' suggests the league leader, but it is the self.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull oneself together is an idiom for recovering composure after being upset.

clue.text: Lie about secure provision for the smarter patrons?

parts.note: to lounge is to lie about lazily
to bar a door is to secure it

explanation.surface: Lazing about while making arrangements for wealthy guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a British pub, once dearer and aimed at a better-off clientele.

clue.text: Joins embassy staff

definitions.meaning: attachés are specialists on an ambassador's staff

explanation.surface: Someone joining an embassy's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach is to connect; an attaché is a diplomatic official, and the plural shares the spelling.

clue.text: Get caught after police knock off

indicators.note: the getting caught comes after the police in the answer

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
something that lodges gets stuck or caught somewhere

explanation.surface: A suspect nabbed after the police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock off' reads as stealing or a police arrest; it means dislodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something off a ledge is to dislodge it from its place.

clue.text: Unit at large performing survey

indicators.note: letters performing put on a show in a new arrangement, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military unit on the loose carrying out reconnaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at large' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'performing' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangulation measures angles from fixed points to map land, the standard method of surveying.

clue.text: Shout down my left ear at first

parts.note: heck! is an exclamation like my!

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone yelling into a person's left ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a speaker with shouts, trying to drown them out.

clue.text: Conservative needs unusual sensitivity, ousting almost all ministers

indicators.note: the shortened word is ousted, pushed out of the sensitivity

parts.note: an allergy is an abnormal sensitivity to something

indicators.note: almost all of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory with odd sensitivities replacing nearly every member of the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' suggests government, but means clergy; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers of religion, priests and pastors, collectively make up the clergy.

clue.text: Rod's tipple laced with unknown ingredient

definitions.note: read as 'Rod is': the definition is Rod, joined to the wordplay by 'is'

indicators.note: a drink laced with something has it slipped into it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: ale is a tipple, an alcoholic drink
X is the algebraic unknown, here the mystery ingredient

explanation.surface: Someone called Rod has had his beer spiked with something mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, with ''s' standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Lots such as furniture maker might bid for?

definitions.text: such as furniture maker might bid for?
definitions.meaning: deal is pine or fir timber, so a cabinetmaker would bid for great deal at auction

explanation.surface: Auction lots that a furniture maker might want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' sounds like the auction items in the scene, but it is the definition meaning plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A great deal is an idiom for a large quantity; deal is also softwood planking used by joiners.

clue.text: Anguish at heart of alien realm

indicators.note: the anguish sits at the heart of the alien, inside it

parts.note: ET is the film's extraterrestrial
gyp is informal British for pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: Pain at the core of a foreign kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country, and was an ancient kingdom of the pharaohs.

clue.text: Fine bird, one for the table

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on a pencil grade
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A fine bird served at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl means poultry such as chicken raised for eating.

clue.text: Canadian water hounds worried by horse

indicators.note: hounds worried are troubled and shaken up, so their letters are scrambled

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs harassed by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' suggests the dogs are anxious, but it rearranges HOUNDS into HUDSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson Bay is the vast inland sea in north-east Canada.

clue.text: Worker using kitchen roller about to leave

indicators.note: the short word for about is told to leave, so it is taken out of the wave

parts.note: a roller is a big wave, also called a breaker
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cook with a rolling pin about to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitchen roller' looks like a rolling pin, but 'roller' is a wave and 'kitchen' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is a tradesperson whose work happens in a kitchen or bakehouse.

clue.text: Immense distance once covered by rodents from the East

indicators.note: the old measure is covered by the rodents, so it sits inside them
in an across entry, coming from the East means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: rats are rodents
an ell was an old measure of length, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: A huge stretch once overrun by rats arriving from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Backwards RATS gives STAR, which surrounds ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar is used informally for something exceptional or enormous in scale.

clue.text: Times added to article about Queen using such means

indicators.note: Times is added to the end of what comes before it
the article goes about the Queen, so it is wrapped round her letters

parts.note: THE is the definite article
ER is Elizabeth Regina
BY means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on the monarch appended to The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means multiplied by.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that method or as a result of that action.
